items.name: Learn Claude Code
items.plainPurpose: This item provides a guide and examples to help you understand how to build your own programs that act like a computer helper.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to see how a computer helper program is built and how it works from the inside.
items.example: Example: You want to learn how to make a computer program that can read files and follow your instructions to finish a task.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will copy the guide files from the internet to a folder on your computer so you can read them and learn from them.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Karpathy Skills
items.plainPurpose: This item adds a set of rules that help your AI agent, which is your computer helper, think more carefully and keep things simple when writing code.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want your computer helper to ask more questions instead of guessing and to avoid making things too complicated.
items.example: Example: You are worried that the computer helper will write too much confusing code, and you want it to make only the small, necessary changes.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will copy the rule files to your computer so your AI agent can follow these guidelines while it works.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Superpowers
items.plainPurpose: This item gives your AI agent a step-by-step way to plan, test, and build software projects correctly.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want a structured way to build a new project from the first idea to the finished product.
items.example: Example: You have a big idea for a new app and you want the helper to brainstorm with you, make a plan, and test everything as it builds.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will add the special planning and testing tools to your AI agent program on this computer.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Ponytail
items.plainPurpose: This item makes your AI agent act like a very experienced person who tries to write as little code as possible to solve a problem.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to save time and keep your computer programs simple by only writing what is absolutely necessary.
items.example: Example: You ask for a way to pick a date on a website, and the helper uses a simple tool already built into the browser instead of building a new one.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will install the special rules into your AI agent using a tool called npx, which is a way to run programs from the internet.
items.userAction: You need to have a program called Node.js, which lets your computer run certain types of code, installed for this to work.

items.name: gstack
items.plainPurpose: This item sets up a full team of virtual experts, like a manager and a designer, to help your AI agent build and launch software.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want your computer helper to act like a whole team of people working together instead of just one person.
items.example: Example: You want one virtual person to plan the work, another to check for mistakes, and another to help you show the project to the public.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will install three programs called Node.js, Git, and Bun, which help your computer run code and track changes, and then set up the virtual team tools.
items.userAction: This setup is not available for Windows computers yet, and you still need to set up the features for your own project.

items.name: ECC
items.plainPurpose: This item adds a complete system for planning, testing, and remembering important information to your AI agent.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want a very organized system that learns from its work and gets better the more you use it.
items.example: Example: You want the helper to remember your favorite ways of working and to check for safety every time it makes a change to your files.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will add the organized system tools to your AI agent program on this computer.
items.userAction: You need to have Node.js version 18 or newer, a tool called Git for tracking changes, and the Claude Code program version 2.1 or newer installed.

items.name: taste-skill
items.plainPurpose: This tool helps the computer build websites that look professional and beautiful. It stops the computer from making boring or generic designs.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want your new website to have better layouts, colors, and fonts that don't look like a computer made them.
items.example: Example: You are building a landing page for a new business and you want it to look like a high-end magazine instead of a basic template.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will download and add design rules to your computer so the helper can use them. It uses a special tool called npx, which is a way to run software from the internet without installing it first, to fetch the files.
items.userAction: This tool uses the MIT license, which is a set of rules that lets you use the software for free. You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Anthropic Skills
items.plainPurpose: This is a collection of official instructions that teach the computer how to handle specific tasks like making Word documents or slide shows.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want the computer to get better at creating and editing files like spreadsheets, which are digital tables for numbers, and presentations.
items.example: Example: You need to turn a messy list of notes into a professional-looking slide show with a specific layout.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds a list of official skills to your computer's organizer. You will be able to pick and install the specific skills you want later.
items.userAction: This tool uses the Apache 2.0 license, which is a set of rules that lets you use the software for free. You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: wshobson/agents
items.plainPurpose: This is a large library of pre-made helpers and skills for many different jobs like coding or checking for security problems.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you need a specialized helper for a specific programming task or a complex technical job.
items.example: Example: You are starting a new project and want a helper that already knows the best ways to test and organize your code.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds a large catalog, or list, of community-made tools to your computer. You can then choose which specific helper or skill you want to install.
items.userAction: This tool uses the MIT license, which is a set of rules that lets you use the software for free. You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Claude Plugins Official
items.plainPurpose: This is the main directory for high-quality add-ons, which are extra tools you can add to a program, that are managed by the people who built the computer's brain.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to browse and find official tools that have been checked for quality and safety.
items.example: Example: You want to find a reliable tool that helps the computer review your code or design new parts of a website.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the official list of add-ons to your computer's organizer. It does not install any specific tools until you pick them yourself.
items.userAction: This tool uses the Apache-2.0 license, which is a set of rules that lets you use the software for free. You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Frontend Design
items.plainPurpose: This tool helps you create the visual parts of a website that people see and click on. It makes the website look professional and unique instead of looking like a computer made it.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to build a new website page that looks great and is easy for people to use.
items.example: Example: You want to make a new page for your personal blog that has special colors and nice-looking buttons.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will add this design tool to your computer so it can help you write the code for how your website looks.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Code Review
items.plainPurpose: This tool looks at the computer instructions you wrote to find mistakes or ways to make them better. It acts like a second pair of eyes to check your work before you share it.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you have finished writing some code and want to make sure there are no hidden errors before you save it.
items.example: Example: You just finished a new feature for a program and want to check if you missed any small bugs that might cause problems later.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will put this checker tool on your computer so it can look at your code and give you helpful tips.
items.userAction: You need to have a GitHub account (a website where people store and share their computer code) and sign in to use this feature.

items.name: Context7
items.plainPurpose: This tool finds the latest instruction manuals for the computer parts you are using. It makes sure the help you get is up-to-date and not based on old information.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you are working with a new piece of software and need to see the newest rules on how to use it correctly.
items.example: Example: You are trying to use a new map feature in your app and want to see the latest examples of how other people did it.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will add this manual-finder to your computer so it can look up the newest guides for you.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Skill Creator
items.plainPurpose: This tool helps you teach your computer assistant new ways to help you. You can use it to build, test, and improve the special tasks you want the assistant to do.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to create a new shortcut or a special way for your computer assistant to handle a specific job.
items.example: Example: You want to teach your assistant a new way to automatically organize your photos every time you save them.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will install this creation tool on your computer so you can start teaching your assistant new tricks.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: UI UX Pro Max
items.plainPurpose: This tool gives the computer expert knowledge about how to design apps and websites that are easy for people to use.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you are building an app and want it to follow professional design rules for colors, buttons, and spacing.
items.example: Example: You are making a health app and want the computer to suggest a calming color scheme and fonts that are easy to read.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will copy a folder of design instructions and scripts, which is called a repository, to your computer. These instructions help the computer understand how to build better interfaces.
items.userAction: This tool uses the MIT license, which is a set of rules that lets you use the software for free. You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Awesome Claude Skills
items.plainPurpose: This is a curated list of many different skills and resources that people have shared to make the computer more capable.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to explore a wide variety of tools and instructions created by other people for different tasks.
items.example: Example: You are looking for a skill that helps the computer create animations or one that knows how to use specific scientific libraries.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI will download a reference list of skills, which is stored in an online folder called a repository, to your computer. It allows you to see what is available and choose which ones to add.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Planning with Files
items.plainPurpose: This tool makes three special files on your computer to save your plans and notes. This helps the computer remember what you are doing even if it turns off or you clear the screen.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to save your progress on a big task so you can finish it later without starting over.
items.example: Example: You are writing a long story and want the computer to remember which chapters you already finished.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI uses a special command to add this planning ability to your computer.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Claude-Mem
items.plainPurpose: This tool saves a summary of your work in a small database, which is like a digital filing cabinet on your computer. It helps the computer remember your past sessions so it knows what you have already done.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want the computer to remember your previous work sessions so you don't have to repeat yourself.
items.example: Example: You fixed a problem with your email yesterday and want the computer to remember that fix when you work on it again today.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI uses a special command to install this memory tool on your computer.
items.userAction: You need to sign in with your email address in a web browser to get a special memory key for your account, but you do not need a credit card.

items.name: CodeGraph
items.plainPurpose: This tool builds a map of all the files in your project and how they connect to each other. This map helps the computer find the right information quickly without reading every single file.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you have a lot of files and want the computer to understand how they all fit together.
items.example: Example: You want to know which parts of your program will change if you move a single file to a new folder.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI downloads and installs the mapping program on your computer.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Graphify
items.plainPurpose: This tool turns your project files into a picture that looks like a web of connections. You can open this picture in your web browser to see how different parts of your work are linked.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to see a visual chart of your project instead of just reading a list of files.
items.example: Example: You are looking at a complicated project and want to see a map of how the main page connects to the database.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI uses a special command to add this graphing ability to your computer.
items.userAction: You might need to provide a secret key, which is like a password, if you want the tool to read documents or videos.

items.name: Repomix
items.plainPurpose: This tool packs all the files in your project into one single file. It also counts the tokens, which are small pieces of text, to make sure the whole project fits into the computer's memory.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to put your entire project into one file so it is easier to share or review.
items.example: Example: You want to send your whole project to a friend so they can look at all your work at once.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI installs the packing tool and sets up its reviewed connection to your local tools.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Convex for Claude Code
items.plainPurpose: This tool helps you build and manage a place to store your app's information, like a digital filing cabinet that updates itself instantly.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want your app to save information and show it to other people right away.
items.example: Example: You are building a shared shopping list app where everyone sees when someone adds milk to the list.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI installs the reviewed Convex helper on this computer. It may then ask you to connect it to a project.
items.userAction: You need to sign in to your Convex account and connect this tool to your specific project.

items.name: Multica
items.plainPurpose: This tool is like a project manager that helps human workers and smart computer programs work together on the same tasks.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to give tasks to smart computer programs just like you would give them to a human coworker.
items.example: Example: You want to tell a computer program to fix a bug in your code while you go for a walk, and see its progress on a board.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI copies the reference files to your computer. It does not install Docker or Make.
items.userAction: You need to install Docker, which is a way to run programs in their own safe boxes, and Make, which is a tool for building software.

items.name: Firecrawl
items.plainPurpose: This tool acts like a smart reader that can visit websites and turn their information into a simple list that computer programs can understand.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you need to get information from a website and use it in your own project.
items.example: Example: You want to gather the latest news headlines from a website to show them in your own daily summary app.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI installs the reviewed helper program on this computer. It does not create or enter a Firecrawl key.
items.userAction: You need to get a special key from the Firecrawl website to prove you are allowed to use their service.

items.name: CC Switch
items.plainPurpose: This tool is a control panel that lets you quickly change which smart computer service is powering your coding tools.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to switch between different companies that provide the brains for your coding assistant.
items.example: Example: You want to stop using one expensive computer brain service and start using a cheaper one with just one click.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI installs the control-panel program only when your computer type is supported.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Vibe Kanban
items.plainPurpose: This tool provides a visual board to help you plan and review work that smart computer programs are doing for you.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to see all your tasks as cards on a board and watch computer programs finish them.
items.example: Example: You have five different computer programs writing code for you at once and you want to see which ones are done.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI leaves this item off because its source is sunsetting; no install will run.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: GitHub MCP
items.plainPurpose: This tool connects your coding assistant to your online storage for code so it can read and write files there for you.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want your coding assistant to help you manage your files and projects on the GitHub website.
items.example: Example: You want the computer to read a list of tasks from your online project and start writing the code to finish them.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI leaves this item off until a safe sign-in path is available; no install will run.
items.userAction: You need to sign in to your GitHub account or provide a special secret token, which is like a long password for your account.

items.name: Playwright MCP
items.plainPurpose: This tool allows your AI assistant to use a web browser to find information on websites. It reads the code of the page—the hidden instructions that build a website—to understand what is there, which is much faster than looking at pictures.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want your AI assistant to browse the internet, check live websites, or test if a website is working correctly.
items.example: Example: You ask the assistant to find the current price of a book on an online store or to check if a login button on your website is in the right place.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI registers the Playwright server so your AI can use it. It adds the necessary settings to your AI configuration—the list of tools it knows how to use—but does not start browsing until you ask it to.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Claude Code Router
items.plainPurpose: This is a control center that helps you manage different AI services in one place. It works like a traffic controller, sending your requests to the best AI provider and keeping track of your usage.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you use several different AI accounts and want one easy way to switch between them or keep them all organized.
items.example: Example: You have accounts with two different AI companies and want to use one single tool to talk to whichever one is faster or cheaper at the moment.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI installs the router software—a program that directs information—on your computer so you can run it whenever you need. It sets up the main program but does not connect your private accounts for you.
items.userAction: You need to provide your own API keys, which are secret passwords for AI services, and set up your providers in the router's dashboard after it is installed.

items.name: Awesome MCP Servers
items.plainPurpose: This is a big list of many different tools that AI assistants can use. It is like a library where you can find extra skills for your AI, such as connecting to databases—digital filing cabinets for large amounts of information—or reading special types of files.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to find new ways to expand what your AI assistant can do and want to see a list of tested options.
items.example: Example: You want your AI to be able to read your calendar or talk to a specific database, and you need to find the right tool to make that happen.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI downloads a copy of this tool library to your computer so you can browse through all the available options easily.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: System Prompts AI
items.plainPurpose: This is a collection of the secret instructions that the AI follows to do its work. It shows you exactly what the AI is told to do when it writes code or plans a task.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to see the hidden rules the AI uses to understand your requests.
items.example: Example: You are curious about how the AI knows which files to look at first and want to read its internal guidebook.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI makes a copy of these instructions on your computer for you to read.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Claude Code Best Practice
items.plainPurpose: This is a library of tips and real examples that show you the best ways to work with the AI. It helps you learn how to give better instructions and organize your work.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to learn smarter ways to use the AI to build your projects.
items.example: Example: You want to see how other people successfully used the AI to fix bugs or start a new project from scratch.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI makes a copy of this guide on your computer so you can look through the examples.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Codex in Claude
items.plainPurpose: This lets you use the AI's coding tools inside a separate program called Codex. It helps you manage your work from one place if you already use that app.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to use the AI tools while working inside the Codex application.
items.example: Example: You use the Codex app for your daily work and want to run AI code reviews without leaving that screen.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI does not turn this on yet because it needs you to have the other program ready first.
items.userAction: You need to have a Codex account and sign in to that app to use this.

items.name: Claude HUD
items.plainPurpose: This adds a small status bar at the bottom of your screen that shows what the AI is doing. It tracks how much memory the AI is using and how far it has gotten with your tasks.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to see a live update of the AI's progress and memory usage while you work.
items.example: Example: You are working on a big project and want to make sure the AI does not run out of room to remember your instructions.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds this status bar to your AI tool.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Caveman
items.plainPurpose: This makes the AI talk in very short, simple sentences. By using fewer words, the AI uses less power and costs less money to run.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want the AI to give you short answers to save on costs.
items.example: Example: You want to save money while asking the AI many small questions, so you tell it to stop using polite filler words.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI makes a copy of this simple-talking tool on your computer.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: convex-orchestrator
items.plainPurpose: This tool helps your computer program follow a list of steps that need to happen in order, even if the computer restarts or stops working for a moment.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you have a long list of tasks for your website, like sending a welcome email and then waiting a few days to check if someone signed up.
items.example: Example: You want to send a "Thank You" note right after someone joins your club, but wait until they confirm their email before giving them a special badge.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the component package only inside the selected project folder. It can prepare the Node.js (a tool that lets your computer run website code) and package.json (a file that lists all the tools your project uses) if required, but it does not set up the feature for you.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: Browserbase Stagehand
items.plainPurpose: This lets you tell a computer program to look at websites and find information or click buttons just by using normal English sentences.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want your website to automatically find and copy information from other websites without you having to click everything yourself.
items.example: Example: You want to automatically check the price of a specific toy on three different store websites every morning.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the component package only inside the selected project folder. It can prepare the Node.js (a tool that lets your computer run website code) and package.json (a file that lists all the tools your project uses) if required, but it does not set up the feature for you.
items.userAction: You need a Browserbase account, a project identification number, and an API key (a secret code that identifies you) to use this service.

items.name: AI Agent
items.plainPurpose: This helps you build smart computer helpers that can remember what you said before and use information to answer your questions.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to add a smart chat box to your website that can help people by looking up information in your files.
items.example: Example: You want a helper on your website that can answer questions about your club's rules by reading the handbook you uploaded.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the component package only inside the selected project folder. It can prepare the Node.js (a tool that lets your computer run website code) and package.json (a file that lists all the tools your project uses) if required, but it does not set up the feature for you.
items.userAction: You still need to read the source page and set up the feature for your own project.

items.name: DatabaseChat
items.plainPurpose: This lets people ask questions about the information stored on your website using simple English instead of complicated computer code.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want to let your team ask questions like "how many people joined today?" without them needing to know how the computer stores data.
items.example: Example: A manager wants to ask their computer "show me all the orders from last week" and get a list right away.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the component package only inside the selected project folder. It can prepare the Node.js (a tool that lets your computer run website code) and package.json (a file that lists all the tools your project uses) if required, but it does not set up the feature for you.
items.userAction: You need an OpenRouter API key (a secret code that lets the computer talk to smart AI models) to make this work.

items.name: Exa
items.plainPurpose: This lets your website search the internet to find fresh news, company information, or specific facts to help answer questions.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want your smart website helper to be able to look up new information on the web that it doesn't already know.
items.example: Example: You want your website to find the latest news articles about space travel and show them to your visitors.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the component package only inside the selected project folder. It can prepare the Node.js (a tool that lets your computer run website code) and package.json (a file that lists all the tools your project uses) if required, but it does not set up the feature for you.
items.userAction: You need an Exa account and an API key (a secret code that lets you use their search service) to use this.

items.name: firecrawl
items.plainPurpose: This tool helps your website search and copy information from entire websites very quickly so it can use that data later.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you need to copy a lot of information from a website, like all the pages of a manual, so your smart helper can read them.
items.example: Example: You want to copy all the instructions from a cooking website so your program can help you find recipes by ingredient.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the component package only inside the selected project folder. It can prepare the Node.js (a tool that lets your computer run website code) and package.json (a file that lists all the tools your project uses) if required, but it does not set up the feature for you.
items.userAction: You need a Firecrawl API key (a secret code that lets you use their web copying service) and may need to set up a webhook secret (a way to safely receive data back).

items.name: SiteGPT
items.plainPurpose: This adds a smart helper to your website that is trained specifically on your own information to answer questions for your visitors.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you want a chat box that already knows everything about your products or services and can help customers 24 hours a day.
items.example: Example: You want a helper that can tell customers exactly what your store's return policy is without you having to answer the same question every time.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the component package only inside the selected project folder. It can prepare the Node.js (a tool that lets your computer run website code) and package.json (a file that lists all the tools your project uses) if required, but it does not set up the feature for you.
items.userAction: You need a SiteGPT account and an API token (a secret code that connects your website to your smart helper).

items.name: Browser Use
items.plainPurpose: This lets a smart computer program use a web browser just like a person would, including logging into accounts and moving through different pages.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you need to automate a task that requires logging into a website or clicking through many different screens.
items.example: Example: You want your program to log into your social media account and post a message for you every Tuesday.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the component package only inside the selected project folder. It can prepare the Node.js (a tool that lets your computer run website code) and package.json (a file that lists all the tools your project uses) if required, but it does not set up the feature for you.
items.userAction: You need a Browser Use Cloud API key (a secret code that lets the computer use the browser service).

items.name: Durable Agents
items.plainPurpose: This helps you build smart helpers that can keep working on a task for a long time, even if the internet cuts out or the computer needs to restart.
items.chooseWhen: Choose this when you have a very big task for an AI that might take a few minutes and you don't want it to fail if there is a small glitch.
items.example: Example: You want an AI to read a very long book and summarize every chapter, which might take longer than a normal quick response.
items.cctiAction: After you approve, CCTI adds the component package only inside the selected project folder.
